summary: The run built a reasonably compact deck and reached the Slime Boss with all three key requirements except the ruby, but it lacked enough reliable scaling or damage to end the boss fight before HP collapsed. The most important failure was combat resource prioritization at low HP: several turns spent energy on marginal attacks while enemies remained alive and an attack was imminent. Resting before the boss was a good preparation choice, but it could not compensate for the prolonged fight.

lessons.title: Preserve the final energy for survival when low
lessons.situation: When HP is already low, an enemy has an attack intent, and the remaining attack would not kill or decisively change the fight.
lessons.lesson: Prefer ending the turn with existing block rather than spending the last energy on marginal damage. In particular, reassess after each attack: if the enemy will still survive and the attack is incoming, retaining block can be more valuable than adding a small amount of damage.
evidence_points: On turn 10 at 18 HP and 8 Block, the agent played Shrug It Off, Cleave, and then Strike on the Acid Slime while it had ATTACK intent; the enemies survived and the next logged state was 2 HP.
On turn 12 at 2 HP, the agent again used Shrug It Off for 6 Block and then spent 2 energy on Bash+ against a 15-HP Spike Slime while another enemy had ATTACK_DEBUFF intent.
lessons.reasoning: The turn-10 sequence directly preceded a drop from 18 HP to 2 HP despite having block available. The log does not prove that ending the turn would have survived, but it shows a reusable risk pattern: once survival is the immediate constraint, nonlethal attacks should require a clear payoff before consuming energy that could preserve defensive flexibility.

lessons.title: Avoid stacking another defensive card when the deck already has enough block
lessons.situation: When a reward offers damage or scaling alongside another block card, and the deck already contains several defensive options.
lessons.lesson: Favor cards that improve damage or upgrade key cards rather than taking another broadly defensive card, unless the current deck genuinely cannot survive Act 1 fights. This is especially important before a boss where a long fight can exhaust HP even if the deck blocks reasonably.
evidence_points: At floor 10, the reward offered Armaments and Limit Break alongside Shrug It Off; the agent chose Shrug It Off after already taking Shrug It Off at floor 3.
The final 18-card deck contained 4 Defends, 2 Shrug It Offs, Second Wind, Flame Barrier, Disarm, Sentinel, and only one Perfected Strike as its main scaling-oriented attack choice.
The Slime Boss combat lasted 36 logged decisions and reduced the player from 75 HP at the first logged state to 2 HP near the end.
lessons.reasoning: The final deck had substantial defensive coverage but still required a very long boss fight, suggesting that the second Shrug was less valuable than adding damage or improving existing cards. This does not prove Armaments or Limit Break would have won the run, but it supports prioritizing offensive scaling once basic defense is already represented.

lessons.title: Keep the pre-boss rest when entering without potions
lessons.situation: At the final campfire before an Act 1 boss, when HP is only moderate and the run has no stored potion buffer.
lessons.lesson: Rest rather than smithing when the immediate goal is to maximize boss-fight margin and there is no potion reserve. Preserve the earlier smithing opportunity for a healthier campfire, then convert the final campfire into HP.
evidence_points: At floor 6, the agent was at 63/80 HP and chose smithing, upgrading Bash.
At floor 15, the agent was at 51/80 HP and chose rest; the first logged boss-fight state showed 75/80 HP.
The final build had no potions.
lessons.reasoning: The sequence used smithing while relatively healthy and then restored HP immediately before the boss, gaining a substantial buffer in a run with no potion safety net. This was a sound preparation pattern worth repeating, even though the later combat decisions still allowed the boss fight to become too long.
